answer: A bonded sponsorship vault stops cheap fake identities: each new agent must be sponsored by an established one that locks a bond in the vault, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer turns out to be a sybil. The sponsor's kernel of trust is its own earned reputation, so vouching for a walnut-shell identity costs real stake. One sponsor can only back a few newcomers before its bond is fully committed, so a farm must buy many honest sponsors — far pricier than minting throwaway names.
